citation.title: Image-Based Multiresolution Topology Optimization Using Deep Disjunctive Normal Shape Model
citation.authors: Vahid Keshavarzzadeh; Mitra Alirezaei; Tolga Tasdizen; Robert M. Kirby
citation.version_coded: version of record, author-institution repository copy

included.method_family: other: deep disjunctive normal shape model

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For the three-dimensional example, generating optimized designs with DDNSM initial guesses takes roughly half the computational time of direct SIMP optimization.
claim.key_phrase: reduces the computational time to almost half
claim.location: Section 5, conclusion; numerical values in Table 13
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Table 13: 92.00 h SIMP / 49.50 h DDNSM, both for 10,000 3D designs and with DDNSM training included = 1.8586.
claim.alternatives: Table 6: 10,000 L-bracket designs take 5.61 h SIMP versus 3.18 h DDNSM with training; Table 15: 1,000 3D designs take 86.65 h SIMP versus 55.96 h DDNSM.

baseline.classical_method: Density-based SIMP with optimality-criteria updates (Sections 2 and 4)
baseline.implementation: 2D: 88-line MATLAB code (Section 2); 3D: MATLAB code of Liu and Tovar [79] (Section 4.3)
baseline.hardware_classical: Intel 12 Core i7-5930K @ 3.5 GHz CPU, 32 GB RAM; sequential CPU processing (Section 4.1, computational time analysis)
baseline.hardware_ml: 2x Intel 8 Core E5-2660 @ 2.20 GHz, 64 GB RAM, 2x Nvidia K20 GPUs for deep learning; subsequent TO on CPU (Section 4.1, computational time analysis)
baseline.problem_size: Primary 3D example: 40 x 20 x 10 high resolution elements and 20 x 10 x 5 low resolution elements (Figure 33); 10,000 designs (Table 13)
baseline.classical_iterations: 152.08 average for direct 3D optimization (Section 4.3, computational cost analysis)
baseline.ml_time: 49.50 h for 10,000 3D designs, including training and refinement (Table 13); 46.15 h without training
baseline.training_time: Included in 49.50 h versus 46.15 h without training (Table 13); 1,639.25 s for 2D L-bracket Case 2 (Section 4.1)
baseline.data_generation_cost: 4.1365e5 FEA cost units for 3D Case 6 training data (Eq. 30); 260.31 s for 2D L-bracket Case 2 (Section 4.1)
baseline.quality_metric: FEM compliance of reconstructed and refined designs relative to directly optimized designs; iteration counts and compliance success rates (Section 4.1; Tables 1, 12)
baseline.quality_gap: 3D Case 6: 83.5% success in compliance estimation and mean 76.28 refinement iterations versus 152.08 direct iterations (Table 12); no single matched-quality gap for Table 13's timing aggregate

R1.evidence: Section 4.3 and Table 12 give FE compliance success rates and refinement to an optimized design, but Table 13 timing is not restricted to cases whose returned compliance and volume meet a matched-quality tolerance.

R2.evidence: Section 4.1 states CPU SIMP and CPU refinement plus GPU training on computers described as similar in computational power; the paper does not establish R2(a)-(e).

R3.evidence: Section 4.1 includes dataset generation, training, network evaluation and refinement in the time accounting; Section 4.3 Eq. (30) calculates break-even at 85 high-resolution 3D designs.

R4.evidence: Sections 4.1 and 4.3 compute FE compliance of predictions and refined designs, and Tables 1 and 12 report success rates, but achieved volume and infeasible or disconnected output rates are not systematically counted.

reporting.n_test_cases: L-bracket: 400 test samples (Section 4.1); 3D: 400 test samples [inferred from Table 12 percentage increments and surrounding text; exact count not stated in 4.3]; heat sink also tested (Section 4.2)

notes: The DDNSM outputs serve as starting designs for further SIMP optimization in the principal timing comparison. Section 4.3 also discusses unrefined predictions, with a much shorter time but weaker verification. No public DDNSM code was stated.
